title: MacPaw taps Liquid AI to offer on-device inference to devs building for its app store
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: MacPaw is building a local version of its AI assistant Eney using Liquid AI's models.
body:
MacPaw, the app developer behind SetApp, has partnered with Liquid AI to integrate on-device artificial intelligence into its products, beginning with its AI assistant, Eney. This collaboration centers on Liquid AI's development of "Elix," an on-device inference system, and a local memory system. Liquid AI's approach involves tailoring model architectures specifically for hardware, ensuring maximum efficiency, enhanced privacy, and robust security by processing AI locally. This design also enables offline functionality for AI assistants and agentic workflows, and crucially, allows models to adapt and improve over time through user interaction.

This initiative holds significant promise for developers and researchers. MacPaw plans to make this local processing architecture available to its developer community, empowering them to build applications leveraging on-device AI inference. This offers compelling advantages like heightened data privacy, strong security, and the ability for AI features to operate without an internet connection. While Apple provides its own local models, Liquid AI highlights its focus on performance across diverse capabilities and customizable models that evolve with use. MacPaw aims to position SetApp as a comprehensive "one-stop shop" for AI development, offering access to both its local AI stack and external cloud models, thereby fostering innovation within its growing app ecosystem.
